# Testing Conventions

Three layers, three purposes. **Do not duplicate coverage across layers** — pick the cheapest layer that proves the behaviour.

**This is not license to skip a component's own test file because its behaviour happens to be
covered transitively elsewhere.** A component with real logic (branching, prop→JSX mapping
decisions, event wiring) gets its own `index.test.ts`/`index.test.tsx`, even when the state it
renders is owned by a hook that already has its own test, or a parent's assembly-level
Storybook `play` already exercises the rendered result. Resolve the duplication concern by
**scoping what that file asserts** — mock the hook/child component whose internals are proven
elsewhere, and test only this component's own contract (given a state, does it render the
right branch; given a DOM event, does it call the right handler) — not by leaving the
component with no test of its own. Relying on a *different* component's story to prove *this*
component's contract means the coverage isn't discoverable from the component's own folder,
and can silently vanish if that unrelated file changes. See
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx` for the
resulting pattern (mocks `useSubscribeSection` and `ZimmSubscribeModal`, tests only its own
render-branch/event-wiring contract). A component with no branching or decision logic at all
(pure prop interpolation, e.g. `BottomBar`) still doesn't need its own suite — the exemption
below for single-parent internal components still applies there.

| Layer | Tool | What it covers | File pattern | CI gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Unit | Vitest | Pure logic, data mapping, transforms, hook behaviour in isolation | `*.test.ts` co-located with the source | Every PR (`qa.yml`) |
| Component interaction | Storybook `play` | User-facing interactions in a single component (clicks, form fills, focus management) | `*.stories.tsx` `play` function | Every PR (`qa.yml`) |
| E2E | Playwright | Full user journeys across pages, multi-region, integration boundaries | `e2e/tests/**/*.spec.{ts,js}` | Every PR (`qa.yml`) — desktop + mobile Chromium against localhost/dev API; BrowserStack multi-browser on `release/**` only |

> Higher-level project rules: [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Testing. Day-to-day file conventions: [conventions.md](./conventions.md). This file describes **how** to write tests at each layer.

---

## What to test (and what to skip)

Write tests where failure would be **non-obvious** or **costly to debug**:

- ✅ Data mapping: Contentful → component props, locale/currency transforms, SFCC payload → view model
- ✅ Integration boundaries: Global-e pricing/tax logic, checkout ownership branching, consent gating
- ✅ Complex state: cart mutations, consent state changes, multi-step flows, optimistic-update rollback
- ✅ Pure logic that would survive a refactor invisibly if broken
- ❌ Re-exports, one-line passthroughs, type-only helpers
- ❌ Storybook visual snapshots — Chromatic/Loki belongs in a separate budget, not Vitest
- ❌ The framework — don't test that React renders, that Chakra applies styles, or that React Query caches

---

## Layer 1 — Vitest (unit)

### File layout

Co-located with the source, `.test.ts` suffix, never `.spec.ts`:

```
overrides/app/utils/formatPrice.ts
overrides/app/utils/formatPrice.test.ts
overrides/app/hooks/useCurrency.ts
overrides/app/hooks/useCurrency.test.ts
```

Components use `index.test.ts` next to `index.tsx` in the component folder
(see [components.md](./components.md) > Components).

### Structure

- `describe` blocks group related cases; `test` (or `it`) for individual cases.
- **Arrange → Act → Assert** pattern, one behaviour per test.
- Test names describe the behaviour, not the implementation: `"converts AUD to USD using the latest Global-e rate"` not `"calls convertCurrency"`.
- Use `beforeEach` for setup; clear mocks with `vi.clearAllMocks()` after each test.

### Mocking

- **Inline mock objects** for isolated unit tests — define plain JS objects right in the test file.
- **`vi.mock()`** for module-level stubs. Mock the smallest possible surface: a single function, not a whole module, when feasible.
- **MSW** is allowed for cross-functional integration tests (multiple modules wired together). Production paths must never depend on MSW — see AGENTS.md > Rules > "No mocking."
- Do not mock the thing under test; do not assert on internal implementation calls when an output assertion would do.
- **Known gap: `ZimmIcon` throws under Vitest.** It imports the base SFCC icons barrel
  (`app/components/icons`), which has a top-level side effect (`AmexSymbol.viewBox = ...`)
  that fails here because SVG imports resolve to raw path strings in this environment, not
  components. Not fixable from a test file — the SVG transform lives in `vitest.config.ts`,
  Tier 1 test config (AGENTS.md Hard Rule 8). Work around it by mocking `ZimmIcon` at the
  smallest surface in any test that renders an icon-consuming component:
  `vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon', () => ({ ZimmIcon: () => null }))` — or,
  if an assertion depends on an accessible name the real `ZimmIcon` would carry (e.g. a
  fallback `<span aria-label>` with no wrapping interactive element), forward the relevant
  props instead of returning `null`. See `footerNavColumn/index.test.tsx` and
  `zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx` for both variants.

### Commerce SDK hooks

Hooks that call `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` (e.g. `useCurrentBasket`, `useCurrentCustomer`) need a `QueryClientProvider` and `CommerceApiProvider` wrapper. Build a small `renderWithProviders` helper in `overrides/app/test-utils/` rather than duplicating wrapper boilerplate per test.

### What NOT to write at this layer

- Visual rendering — that's Storybook
- Cross-page navigation — that's Playwright
- Real network calls — never; use MSW or stubbed hooks

---

## Layer 2 — Storybook `play` (component interaction)

### When to use `play`

Every UI component has a `*.stories.tsx` (see [components.md](./components.md) > Storybook). Add a `play` function when there is **interactive behaviour worth asserting**:

- Form validation triggers on blur / submit
- Disclosure (accordion, drawer, modal) opens / closes via keyboard + mouse
- Focus moves correctly through a flow
- A controlled input's onChange wires through to the rendered output

If the story is purely visual (renders different prop combinations), no `play` is needed.

### Pattern

```tsx
import {expect, userEvent, within} from '@storybook/test'

export const SubmitDisabledUntilValid: Story = {
    play: async ({canvasElement}) => {
        const canvas = within(canvasElement)
        const submit = canvas.getByRole('button', {name: /submit/i})
        await expect(submit).toBeDisabled()
        await userEvent.type(canvas.getByLabelText(/email/i), 'name@example.com')
        await expect(submit).toBeEnabled()
    }
}
```

- Always query through `within(canvasElement)` — never reach into `document` directly.
- Use **`getByRole`** with an accessible name as the first-choice selector. Fall back to `getByLabelText` for form fields, `getByText` last.
- Don't import `userEvent` from `@testing-library/user-event` — use the Storybook re-export so the action is logged in the timeline.
- **Exception — Portal-rendered dialogs (Modal, Drawer).** Chakra's `Modal`/`Drawer` render their
  content via a React Portal that appends directly to `document.body`, outside `canvasElement` —
  and this project's `.storybook/preview.tsx` configures no custom portal container, so there is
  no way to reach that content through `within(canvasElement)`. A `play` function asserting on a
  portaled dialog's content queries `within(document.body)` instead for that assertion, with an
  inline comment citing this exception (see `zimmDrawer/index.stories.tsx`'s `Large` story). This
  is the only sanctioned use of `within(document.body)` at this layer — every other query still
  goes through `within(canvasElement)`.

### What NOT to write at this layer

- Multi-page flows — that's Playwright
- Heavy API mocking — keep stories visual, push integration assertions to Playwright

---

## Layer 3 — Playwright (E2E)

### Workflow

E2E tests follow the **three-stage gherkin-first workflow** (see [.claude/skills/qa-generate/](../skills/qa-generate/SKILL.md)):

1. Claude (or any developer) drafts a `.feature` file with Gherkin scenarios
2. Lead QA validates in plain English — **no Playwright code is written until sign-off**
3. Playwright spec is generated only after the `.feature` is approved

This prevents "technically correct tests of the wrong behaviour."

### File layout

```
e2e/features/         # Gherkin .feature files — source of truth, reviewed by Lead QA
e2e/fixtures/         # multi-region fixtures keyed by SITE_ID
e2e/support/
  helpers/            # shared helpers (auth, basket setup)
  pages/              # Page Object Model classes (BasePage, CheckoutPage, …)
e2e/tests/zimm/       # generated Playwright specs, mirroring features/
```

Spec filename convention for story-backed specs: `SFCC-NNN_short-description.<priority>.spec.ts`
(`.p0.` runs in the Digital SIT gate on `release/**`; on a `develop`-targeted PR, `e2e-localhost`
runs only the specs relevant to the diff — see **Change-scoped E2E** below). Jira-less smoke
tests use `SMOKE-{area}-{behaviour}.spec.js` instead — see
[e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) > Smoke tests.

### Change-scoped E2E (`develop`-targeted PRs only)

`e2e-localhost` (`.github/workflows/qa.yml`) narrows which specs it runs based on the changed
files in the diff, instead of always running the full suite:

- Every spec must carry a Playwright test tag matching its Gherkin file's `@area` tag (see
  [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) for the tag list — `homepage`,
  `checkout`, `search`, `account`, `pdp`, `plp`, `integrations`) — and, per **BrowserStack story
  scoping** below, its `@SFCC-NNN` tag too: `test('...', {tag: ['@homepage', '@SFCC-142']}, async
  ({page}) => {...})`. Smoke tests (no Jira story — see
  [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) > Smoke tests) are exempt from the
  `@SFCC-NNN` half of this — `@area @smoke` only.
- `detect-changes`'s `Get changed files` step defines one file-path allow-list per area
  (`e2e_homepage`, and so on as new areas get specs). `Compute E2E scope` narrows the run to
  that area's `--grep` tag **only if every e2e-relevant changed file falls inside that one
  area's allow-list**. A single file outside it (a shared/global path, or one no area has
  claimed yet) resolves to `e2e_scope: skip` instead — `e2e-localhost` does not run at all on
  that PR (changed 2026-08-25, at the developer's request; previously fell back to running the
  full suite on every such PR). `qa.yml`'s inline comments are the source of truth for the exact
  path lists — don't duplicate them here, they'll drift.
- **This is a deliberate coverage trade-off, not a gap to silently work around.** A
  `develop`-targeted PR that can't be scoped to one area gets no PR-time E2E run at all — only
  unit tests / Storybook, plus BrowserStack if the PR references a Jira key with a tagged spec.
  Full/non-P0 regression coverage for that PR is deferred to the existing post-merge P0 gates
  (`deploy-test.yml`'s Test-tier gate, `digital-sit.yml`'s `playwright-p0` on `release/**`) —
  which only cover P0-tagged journeys, a subset of the full suite. A non-P0 regression introduced
  by a shared/global-path change can therefore reach `develop` before anything catches it. This
  was accepted deliberately to stop the full suite running on every PR touching a shared path
  (the single largest line item in this repo's CI-minutes usage) — revisit if it causes real
  regressions to slip through in practice.
- `release/**`-targeted PRs always run the full suite regardless of diff, unchanged — a release
  PR aggregates a whole sprint and gets the supervised, thorough pre-merge treatment per
  [releaseBranchesRules.md](../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md). This skip-instead-of-full
  behavior only applies to `develop`-targeted PRs.
- **Adding a new area's first spec:** give it its own allow-list group in `qa.yml`'s
  `detect-changes` job, tag every `test()` in it with the matching `{tag: '@area'}`, and add it
  to this section. Forgetting either step doesn't lose coverage silently — it just means that
  spec's PRs get `e2e_scope: skip` (no PR-time run) instead of the scoping optimisation, same as
  any other unclaimed path.

### BrowserStack story scoping

`e2e-browserstack` is Zephyr-linked per-story execution, not a general regression gate — that's
what `e2e-localhost` and the Digital SIT gate are for. It's split across **two** workflows, by
target branch (2026-08-25 cost review — see "What `e2e-browserstack` actually tests against"
below for why):

- **`.github/workflows/qa.yml`** — `release/**` PRs. Runs inline alongside the rest of `QA`,
  full suite, unscoped, always against the static `test` tier (no per-branch preview exists for
  a `release/**`/`fix/release-*` branch — see below).
- **`.github/workflows/e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`** — `develop`-targeted PRs. A separate,
  `workflow_run`-triggered workflow, event-driven off `deploy-preview.yml`'s completion (see
  below for why it isn't just another `qa.yml` job).

Both name their one job identically (`Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)`), which
`zephyr-results-sync.yml` relies on below.

**How results actually reach Zephyr (SFCC-751).** BrowserStack's own native Jira/Zephyr
integration cannot do this — it only supports US/EU Zephyr API regions, and this org's Zephyr
Scale instance is DE-hosted (confirmed via BrowserStack's Quality Engineering Insights setup
flow, which has no field for a custom Zephyr API host). Instead, `.github/workflows/zephyr-
results-sync.yml` runs after every completed run of **either** `QA` or `Cross-browser E2E
(BrowserStack Preview)` (`workflow_run` watches both): it reads that run's BrowserStack build via
the Test Observability API (`GET /ext/v1/builds/{id}/testRuns` — the one endpoint with a real
per-test `tags` field; classic Automate's `builds.json`/`sessions.json` has none), and for every
result tagged `@zephyr:KEY` (see [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md)), posts a
Pass/Fail execution to Zephyr. On failure, it also files a Jira defect against the `@SFCC-NNN`
story directly via Jira's API — BrowserStack's own "Report a bug" flow is manual-UI-only,
confirmed no CLI/API/MCP path exists for automatic-on-failure filing. Zephyr's REST API has no
attachment endpoint at all (confirmed via multiple SmartBear community threads), so failure
evidence (BrowserStack session link, error text) goes on the Jira defect, not the Zephyr
execution. See `scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs`'s doc comment for the full mechanism.

**Both `zephyr-results-sync.yml` and `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` only exist once merged.**
GitHub only evaluates a `workflow_run`-triggering workflow's own definition from the repository's
**default branch** — a copy of either file sitting only on a feature/PR branch is invisible to
GitHub Actions entirely (doesn't even appear in `gh workflow list`) and will never fire, no matter
what happens on that PR. This also means neither workflow can be tested end-to-end against a real
PR before that PR merges — plan around this rather than expect a pre-merge dry run of the trigger
itself (each workflow's underlying *script*/*steps* logic can still be exercised independently —
`scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs` locally against a real BrowserStack build,
`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`'s BrowserStack run itself via `npm run test:story` — just not the
`workflow_run` trigger). `zephyr-results-sync.yml` deliberately does **not** check out
`github.event.workflow_run.head_sha` — a `workflow_run` job carries real secrets regardless of who
triggered the original run, so checking out and executing a PR branch's own version of
`scripts/*.mjs` at that ref would let a modified script on the branch exfiltrate credentials
directly. It checks out the default branch instead (no `ref:` override), which costs nothing given
the above. `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` **does** check out the triggering run's `head_sha` — it
has to, to run that PR's own `e2e/tests/zimm` specs and `scripts/computeBuildName.mjs` — which
carries the same secrets-alongside-PR-code shape `qa.yml`'s `e2e-browserstack` job already had on
`pull_request`; acceptable only because this repo's branches are always same-repo, never a fork
(see [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Branch Rules) — revisit if that ever changes.

**Build naming.** `browserstack.yml`'s `buildName`/`testObservabilityOptions.buildName` are both
derived from the PR's primary Jira key via `scripts/computeBuildName.mjs` (`node
scripts/computeBuildName.mjs SFCC-751` → `3-SFCC-751-SFCC-T285 - <short summary>`, prefixed with
`Sprint-` by the yml template) — a live Jira lookup for the sprint number + issue summary, plus a
grep across `e2e/tests/zimm` for any `@zephyr:` tag on a spec also carrying that Jira key. Only
the `develop`-PR path (`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`) calls this script with a real key —
`qa.yml`'s `release/**` path has no single primary story, so it just uses the plain run number.
Either job uploads the resulting name as a build artifact; `zephyr-results-sync.yml` downloads
that artifact (via `actions/download-artifact` and the triggering run's ID) instead of
recomputing the name itself — it deliberately checks out `develop`, not the PR branch (see the
workflow's own comment), so an independent recompute there would see a different
`e2e/tests/zimm` spec-file set than the triggering job did whenever a PR adds or renames a
Zephyr-tagged spec, and miss the build lookup entirely until the PR merges. An earlier version of
this paragraph described that as a small, accepted drift risk from calling the script
independently in both jobs — corrected 2026-08-25 (CodeRabbit, PR #61): the risk was real and
guaranteed for exactly this kind of PR, not rare, so it's fixed via artifact-passing instead of
documented as accepted. The download failing is only treated as "nothing to sync" when
`e2e-browserstack` never ran for that triggering run at all (checked via the Actions API); if that
job DID run and the artifact is still missing, the sync job fails loudly instead of guessing a
fallback name that could silently miss a real BrowserStack build (CodeRabbit flagged this
correctly, 2026-08-25).

**Desktop/mobile project isolation — a real gotcha, not a style choice.** BrowserStack Test
Observability groups results by test *title* across what it calls "reruns," regardless of which
Playwright project produced them. A spec whose desktop assertions pass on `chromium` and whose
mobile assertions are skipped or fail on `mobile-chrome` — if both share one test title — collapses
to a single dashboard row showing only the *last-recorded* status, silently hiding whichever
result didn't "win" (confirmed against real build data, SFCC-751, 2026-08-25 — a build with 11
real chromium passes and 11 skipped mobile-chrome entries under identical titles showed
`passed: 0, skipped: 11` via BrowserStack's own API, not just the dashboard UI). `test.skip()`
does not avoid this — the skipped entry still shares the title and still clobbers.

The only real fix is to stop the "wrong" project from ever collecting that test at all, which
`playwright.config.js`'s existing per-project `testIgnore` already supports: the `chromium`
project ignores `**/mobile/**`, and `mobile-chrome` ignores `**/desktop/**`. When a spec has
platform-specific assertions that would otherwise share a title across projects, split it into
genuinely separate files under sibling `desktop/`/`mobile/` folders (e.g.
`e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/desktop/SFCC-751_header-nav-site-prefix.spec.js` and
`e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/mobile/SFCC-751_mobile-header-nav-gap.spec.js`) rather than one file with
per-project `test.skip()` branches — that keeps each test's title unique to the one project that
ever runs it for real, so pass/fail on one project can never be overwritten by a skip or a
different result from the other. Same-file-with-distinct-titles was tried and rejected for this
exact reason — the underlying `test()` call is still collected (and skipped) on the other project
regardless of what its title says.

**Access-gated preview URLs.** `BasePage.goto()` supports two optional env vars,
`E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_NAME`/`E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_VALUE`, for a `RETAIL_APP_HOME` that requires a custom
header to reach at all (e.g. an access-gated MRT preview URL) — unset by default, so SIT/
production targets need neither. Not Didomi-specific; a generic single header pair, since that's
the one real case this repo has needed so far.

**What `e2e-browserstack` actually tests against.** Not the static `test` tier by default —
`test` only updates via deliberate tag promotion (see [tagging.md](./tagging.md)), so its
currently-deployed build has no guaranteed relationship to any given PR. On the `develop`-PR path,
`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` downloads the hostname `deploy-preview.yml` persisted as an
artifact on its own run (ephemeral `pr-<slug>` MRT target, deployed on every push to the branch —
see that workflow) and points BrowserStack there — so it's testing this PR's own code.

**No fallback to the static test tier when that artifact is missing (removed 2026-08-26,
CodeRabbit flagged this correctly)** — an earlier version of this job silently fell back to the
static `test`-tier `RETAIL_APP_HOME` whenever `deploy-preview.yml` failed or hadn't finished. That
let a develop PR whose own deployment genuinely failed still produce a green, story-tagged Zephyr
execution (and a possible auto-filed Jira defect) that proved nothing about the PR's own code —
the exact condition the fallback existed to tolerate was the one that made its result meaningless.
`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`'s "Resolve BrowserStack test target" step now fails the job loudly
(`::error::` + `exit 1`) instead when the hostname artifact is missing, whether that's because
Deploy Preview failed outright or succeeded but didn't reach the artifact-upload step. Same
principle [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md)'s Graceful Degradation section already states for
checkout/payment: never silently substitute a different flow, surface an explicit error instead.
A cancelled Deploy Preview run is the one case with nothing to fail loudly about — the job-level
`if:` skips the whole job entirely rather than running it just to hit this failure, since there's
no meaningful error to surface for a run nobody asked to complete.

**This used to be a single job in `qa.yml` that polled for `deploy-preview.yml`'s run to finish —
that design is gone, not just retuned (2026-08-25 cost review).** It started alongside `Deploy
Preview` (both triggered by the same push) and slept in a loop waiting for it, since there was no
other way for one already-running, already-billed job to wait on a *different* workflow's run —
up to ~17 minutes of pure idle runner time per push, worst case, before the real BrowserStack run
even started. (An earlier version of this note described tuning that wait down from a wrongly
inflated 70-minute job timeout / 40-minute poll to 40/15 — that tuning is now moot; the wait
itself no longer exists.) `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` fixes this at the root by being a
separate workflow, `workflow_run`-triggered off `Deploy Preview`'s completion: GitHub fires it
the instant that run finishes, with the run ID and conclusion already in the event payload — no
polling, so no billed wait, ever. `release/**` PRs were never part of this problem —
`deploy-preview.yml` never runs for `fix/release-*` branches, so `qa.yml`'s `e2e-browserstack`
job (which still handles that path) goes straight to the static test tier with nothing to wait
for.

- **`release/**`-targeted PRs (`qa.yml`):** always run the full `e2e/tests/zimm` suite, unscoped.
  A release aggregates a whole sprint's stories, so per-story scoping doesn't apply — Zephyr
  traceability still works, since every test carries its own `@SFCC-NNN` tag individually.
- **`develop`-targeted PRs (`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`):** on `Deploy Preview`'s completion,
  the job finds the open PR for that branch (`gh pr list --head`, one call, no loop) and regexes
  `SFCC-\d+` out of its title, body, and branch name — the same signal the GitHub-for-Jira app
  uses to link a PR to an issue, so this needs no Jira API credentials of its own (duplicated from
  `qa.yml`'s `detect-changes` step rather than shared — the two workflows have no other runtime
  dependency on each other). If at least one key is found, the job runs `--grep`-scoped to that
  story's tag(s) (OR-joined if the PR references more than one). **No key found → the job exits
  without running BrowserStack.** This is deliberate, not a gap: with nothing to attribute results
  to in Zephyr, there's nothing correct to run. It also re-checks `qa.yml`'s own `e2e`-path
  relevance gate before running — a single non-looping artifact download from that commit's `QA`
  run — **but this is a fail-open check, not an unconditional guarantee** (CodeRabbit flagged the
  distinction correctly, 2026-08-26): the normal path is that a Jira-tagged PR touching nothing
  e2e-relevant genuinely skips BrowserStack. If the QA-run lookup or the `e2e-scope` artifact
  download itself fails for any reason (the run isn't found yet, the artifact expired, an API
  hiccup), this step assumes relevant rather than adding a retry loop to chase the optimisation —
  so in that specific failure case, a Jira-tagged PR can still run BrowserStack even when its
  changes weren't e2e-relevant. Worst case is one avoidable BrowserStack run, not a correctness
  problem, but it's a real exception to the "doesn't pay for a BrowserStack run" claim, not a
  universal guarantee.
- If a key is found but no spec carries the matching `@SFCC-NNN` tag, `--grep` matches zero
  tests and Playwright reports "no tests found" without spinning up any BrowserStack sessions
  — a free no-op, not a failure, and not something that falls back to a full run.
- Every story-backed spec needs its Jira key as a tag alongside its `@area` tag (see
  **Change-scoped E2E** above) for this to work — the `qa-generate` skill adds both
  automatically. Jira-less smoke tests (`@area @smoke` only) never match a story key, so they
  correctly never run under BrowserStack — that's expected, not a gap; they're already covered
  by `e2e-localhost`.
- **Local pre-push equivalent:** `npm run test:story` (`scripts/runStoryTests.sh`) runs the
  same `browserstack-node-sdk playwright test e2e/tests/zimm --grep` command against real
  BrowserStack, so a developer can exercise their story before opening the PR. Pass the key
  explicitly (`npm run test:story -- SFCC-142`) or let it auto-detect from commit messages on
  the branch and the branch name — the same `SFCC-\d+` pattern, applied to local git state
  instead of PR title/body since no PR exists yet at that point. Requires `BROWSERSTACK_*` and
  the `E2E_*`/`PWA_E2E_*` vars in `.env` — see `.env.sample`. Manual, not enforced by a git
  hook — relies on developer discipline, not a blocking gate.

### Multi-region fixtures

Build SITE_ID-keyed fixtures from day one — Zimmermann has 8 storefronts across 6 regions (AU, US domestic, US international, UK, EU domestic, EU international, HK, ME) and 11 active locales. Do not retrofit. A test that hardcodes a region or currency cannot survive the rollout.

```ts
test.describe('Guest checkout', () => {
    for (const site of SITES) {
        test(`completes on ${site.id}`, async ({page}) => { ... })
    }
})
```

### Page Object Model

Selector priority — **enforce in code review**. Select elements the way real users (and assistive tech) perceive them:

1. **Accessible selectors** — role with accessible name, label, placeholder, visible text. `getByRole('button', {name: 'Add to bag'})`, `getByLabelText('Email')`, `getByPlaceholderText('Search')`, `getByText('Sale')`. First choice — these double as continuous a11y checks.
2. **Semantic selectors** — standard HTML attributes when no accessible selector applies. `getByAltText('Profile picture')`, `getByTitle('Close modal')`.
3. **Test IDs** — `data-testid` only when the element has no semantic meaning or text content (dynamic containers, canvas elements, loading spinners, complex layout blocks).

Never select by tag name, class name, or DOM position. The priority order keeps tests close to user experience and minimises `data-testid` clutter in the DOM, while still allowing a reliable fallback where semantics genuinely don't exist.

### What NOT to write at this layer

- Pure logic — that's Vitest
- Component interaction in isolation — that's Storybook `play`
- Network-mocked flows — Playwright always hits real SFCC APIs (dev org on feature PRs, SIT on the release gate). Do not stub network calls in Playwright tests.

**Fonts are self-hosted and served on every tier.** `overrides/app/static/fonts/` holds two
Futura Round faces — Regular 400 and Medium 500 — declared by
`overrides/app/theme/fontFace.tsx` and mounted in both `_app-config/index.tsx` and
`.storybook/preview.tsx`. Only two faces exist because only two are used: all 22 textStyles
resolve to fontWeight 400 or 500, and `fonts.body === fonts.heading`.

There is **no environment gate** on this, and it is worth stating plainly because an earlier
revision of this section claimed there was. `ZimmFontFace` mounts unconditionally inside
`_app-config`'s `ChakraProvider`, and `pwa-kit-dev`'s `staticFolderCopyPlugin` copies
`overrides/app/static` in both the client and SSR webpack configs — so the `.woff2` are
published with every bundle and shoppers on every storefront render Futura Round.

`foundation/fonts.ts` already lists `'Futura Round'` first in both stacks, so the `@font-face`
declaration is the only thing that makes it resolve — no component, recipe or token changes.
The fallback stack renders roughly 13% wider, which is why serving the real faces matters for
design-parity review against Figma.

Per-component theme overrides live in `overrides/app/theme/components/` (**Tier 2**) or, per
the co-location pattern, beside their component as `<name>.css.ts` — governed by that
component's own CODEOWNERS entry instead, not this Tier — see
[protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md). `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts`
is also **Tier 2** — it composes the `.zimm-*` global class registry from the `--zimm-*`
variables defined in `foundation/zimmTokens.ts`, so it is derived styling rather than a
brand token source, but it emits CSS on every page and therefore needs a named owner.

# TypeScript Conventions

TypeScript-specific idioms that apply to every `.ts`/`.tsx` file. See
[conventions.md](./conventions.md) for the base "TypeScript only inside `overrides/`" rule
and general cross-cutting conventions; see [components.md](./components.md) for how these
apply specifically to component props and hook signatures.

---

- **No `any`** without an inline comment explaining why a narrower type is impossible.
  Prefer `unknown` with a type guard when the shape is genuinely not known at that point.
- **Prefer `type` over `interface`** for component props, shared shapes, and utility type
  aliases. Use `interface` only when declaration merging is genuinely needed.
- **No non-null assertion (`!`)** without an inline comment explaining why the value is
  guaranteed non-null at that point — same reasoning as the `any` policy. Prefer a proper
  null check, an early return, or narrowing the type instead.
- **Discriminated unions for variant/state modeling.** When a value can be one of several
  distinct shapes (e.g. a basket item that's either a product or a gift card, or a fetch
  state that's loading/error/success), model it as a discriminated union with a common
  literal `kind`/`type` field rather than one type with a pile of optional fields. Lets
  TypeScript narrow correctly in each branch instead of requiring manual `? :` guards.
- **Prefer utility types over hand-rolled duplicate shapes.** `Pick<ProductTileProps, 'id' | 'name'>`,
  `Omit<...>`, `Partial<...>`, `Required<...>` — reach for these before redeclaring a
  near-identical type by hand. A hand-copied type silently drifts from its source when the
  original changes; a utility type doesn't.
- **`import type` for type-only imports.** `import type {ProductTileProps} from './types'` —
  keeps type-only imports from ending up in the compiled bundle and makes the type-vs-value
  distinction explicit at the import site.
- **`satisfies` over a type assertion (`as`)** when you want literal-type inference _and_
  a check that the value conforms to a type — e.g. a config object where you want
  autocomplete on the literal keys but also compiler validation against a shape. Reach for
  `as` only when you're genuinely overriding what TypeScript can infer (and treat that the
  same as an `any` — comment why).
- **`readonly`** on props and arrays that the receiving component/function must not mutate
  — particularly array/object props passed down from a parent that still owns that data.
  Signals intent at the type level instead of relying on convention alone.
- **Generic type parameter naming.** Single-letter (`T`, `K`, `V`) is fine for a generic
  utility with one obvious parameter. Once there's more than one type parameter, or the
  generic's role isn't obvious from context, use a descriptive name prefixed with `T`
  (`TItem`, `TResponse`) so the signature reads clearly without having to trace usage.

  real GitHub org team.
- Branch protection on `develop`/`main`/`release/**` requires an approving code-owner review
  before merge — this is the actual gate, enforced natively by GitHub with no Actions
  involvement, so it can't be affected by a broken or delayed CI run.
- `.github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml`'s `tier1-guard` job posts a loud warning and an
  owner-contact-map on any PR touching a Tier 1 path. It is **not** a required status check —
  GitHub locked down cross-run check-run updates in Feb 2025, which made a "hard-fail until
  approved, then flip to pass on review" required check impossible to implement reliably (a
  fresh commit is needed to re-evaluate it, since a later review can't flip an earlier run's
  result). The CODEOWNERS-based review requirement above is the real, working block.

Because the actual gate lives in GitHub, not in Claude's judgement, this file does not encode
personal names or email addresses as a bypass condition — a string in a shared, version-controlled
file is not an identity check; anyone (or any other Claude session) could satisfy it by typing it.
Instead, Claude may verify the real, authenticated identity behind the current session:

- Before pausing to ask for Tier 1 confirmation, run `gh api user --jq .login`, then check
  `gh api orgs/ZimmermannAU/teams/tier-1-approvers/members --jq '.[].login'` (or check for `admin`
  via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/collaborators/<login>/permission`). If that GitHub
  login is a member of `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` or holds repo admin, Claude may proceed
  with the edit after stating which Tier 1 file is being touched and why — no separate
  confirmation message is required, since GitHub already recognises that account as an approver.
- If the authenticated login is **not** a member/admin, Claude must still stop per Hard Rule #2:
  name the file, and require the developer to secure an approving review from
  `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` before the PR can merge. CODEOWNERS auto-requests that review
  and branch protection blocks the merge without it, regardless of what `tier1-guard` reports.
- This check only ever reduces _how many times Claude pauses to ask_. It changes nothing about
  what GitHub will actually allow to merge — that's deliberate, so a compromised or careless
  Claude session can't grant itself write access to a frozen file.

## Coding Task Workflow

Every coding task follows these four steps in order. Do not skip ahead — pause at the marked points and wait for the user.

1. **Clarify requirements.** Identify every gap, ambiguity, or contradiction in the request and the relevant `.docs/`. Confirm each one with the user before moving on — no assumptions. See Hard Rule #12: ask one question at a time.
2. **Plan.** State the files you intend to touch, _why_ each one is being touched, and any base template files that will need to be copied to `overrides/`. Then **pause** and wait for the user to confirm the plan. See the **Minimal changes** rule below.
3. **Copy first (if any).** For every base template file identified in step 2, follow the **Copy-first rule** in the Rules section. Then **pause** and let the user test and stage the override files before any functional changes.
4. **Implement.** Make the planned modifications. Remove the `console.log` markers from step 3 once the user confirms the overrides are rendering. Before committing a non-trivial code change, run a local CodeRabbit review: confirm the CLI is installed and authenticated (`coderabbit auth status`; if not authenticated, `coderabbit auth login --api-key "$CODERABBIT_API_KEY"` — see `.env.sample`), then `cr review --light --base develop` (use `main` instead on a `release/**`/`hotfix/**` branch). **The CLI is required, not optional** — if it isn't installed or authenticated, stop and have the developer install it (https://www.coderabbit.ai/cli) and run `npm run env -- init` to pull the shared key, rather than committing without a local review. The review itself is still advisory relative to the actual merge gate (the GitHub PR review remains the real gate) — use judgement on whether a flagged finding is worth fixing before the commit vs. leaving it for the PR review to catch, but the review must actually run.

**Responding to a CodeRabbit PR review.** Once CodeRabbit finishes reviewing an open PR, always leave an explicit in-thread reply for every finding, whether it's fixed or not — CodeRabbit's learning feature picks up patterns from PR conversation, so silence teaches it nothing and an explanation teaches it to stop flagging the same non-issue. A fix commit alone, with no reply posted on the thread, doesn't count. For a finding that gets fixed, a short in-thread reply confirming the fix (referencing the commit is fine) is enough. For a finding that is *not* being fixed because it conflicts with this repo's own rules/docs/architecture (e.g. a Tier 1 exception that was actually followed correctly, an intentional design tradeoff already recorded in `.docs/`) — reply in-thread explaining the specific rule or doc that justifies not changing it, so CodeRabbit's learning has the context to recognise the same pattern next time instead of re-flagging it. Never silently dismiss a finding without a reply.

## Multi-site & Routing

The SFCC sites are hard routing and config boundaries — **never bleed config across sites.** Never assume a storefront's routing, URL prefix, checkout ownership, or consent defaults without checking [.docs/prd/regional.md](.docs/prd/regional.md).

## Commands

- `npm start` — local dev at http://localhost:3000. **Do not run!** Ask the user to restart if needed.
- `npm run build`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run push` (Managed Runtime deploy)

## Accessibility

Target WCAG 2.2 AA. Fall back to 2.1 AA only where 2.2 is technically infeasible — document why.

## Rules

*Day-to-day code-writing conventions live in `.claude/rules/` and load automatically:
[conventions.md](.claude/rules/conventions.md) (cross-cutting: naming, imports, DRY, security),
[typescript.md](.claude/rules/typescript.md) (TS idioms), [css.md](.claude/rules/css.md)
(Chakra tokens, `.scss`), and [components.md](.claude/rules/components.md)
(component/hook/utility structure, Storybook categorisation, composition). The rules below
are project-specific behaviours and security guardrails that don't fit there.*

- **No mocking:** All data must come from the live Commerce Cloud API via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hooks. No MSW or hardcoded fixtures in production paths.
- **Environment variables:** Never hardcode secrets, tokens, API keys, or credentials anywhere in the codebase. Local values live in `.env.shared` (tier-independent) and `.env.<tier>` (dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod) — gitignored, managed via `npm run env` (`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`; full command reference in `.env.sample`'s header) — and are set as platform environment variables on Managed Runtime for staging/prod. When adding a new env var: (1) add it to `.env.sample` tagged `# scope:shared|tier|personal|auto` on its own comment line above the key (value only if it's a non-secret public identifier, otherwise leave blank — never a trailing comment, or a blank placeholder reads as non-empty to the pre-commit secret guard), (2) run `npm run env -- init` to scaffold the new key into `.env.shared`/`.env.<tier>`, then fill in the real value locally. Never put tokens, bearer credentials, DSNs, or licence keys in `.env.sample`. Non-personal shared/tier values may additionally be centrally published via `npm run env -- push <scope>` (tier-1-approvers only) to this repo's GitHub Environments — genuinely personal credentials (`scope:personal`, e.g. your own Atlassian or Contentful CMA token) must never be pushed.
- **Comments:** Do not remove existing commented-out code or comments (except when removing the corresponding code) — leave for the user to delete manually. (For _new_ comments introduced in a PR, see conventions.md.)
- **Icons:** Use `overrides/app/components/icons` — this is the single source of truth for all icons (Zimmermann custom and base PWA). Do not import from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons` directly. If a required icon is missing from the overrides set, ask the user — do not substitute a visually different one.
- **Styling:** Chakra UI component props first; use a `.scss` file alongside the component only when Chakra props are insufficient. The `overrides/app/theme/` folder is the source of truth — brand tokens in `foundation/` (Tier 1), one file per component override in `components/` (Tier 2), composed in `index.ts`. Register a new component override in `theme/components/index.ts`.
- **Minimal changes:** Make the smallest change that fully achieves the task. Do not remove or replace existing base template functionality unless explicitly instructed. When a larger change (e.g., a refactor for cleanliness) seems beneficial, propose it and wait for user confirmation — never do it silently.
- **Copy-first rule:** For any task that requires overriding base template files that do not yet exist in `overrides/`, the very first step is to prepare all of them at once: (1) copy each file from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/`, (2) convert each to TypeScript (`.ts`/`.tsx`) and update relevant imports, (3) run `npx tsc --noEmit`, (4) add a temporary `console.log` to each copied file identifying it (e.g. `console.log('[overrides] product-tile.tsx')`) so the user can verify the override is rendering instead of the base component, then **stop and present the converted files to the user to test**. Wait for the user to confirm the overrides are rendering before making any functional changes; remove the `console.log` statements once confirmed. Never skip this step or bundle it silently with functional changes.

## Consent & Marketing

- **Didomi:** Do not load any third-party script until Didomi consent is granted. Gate all analytics, marketing, and tracking scripts behind Didomi callbacks.
- **Marketing opt-in:** Unchecked by default on all storefronts except US (pre-checked). Sync opt-in state: FE → SFCC → Omneo → Emarsys.

_Per-storefront Didomi defaults, GTM/Enhanced Conversions setup, and Inside Chat rules: see [.docs/prd/regional.md](.docs/prd/regional.md)._

## Type Definitions

- **Component-specific prop types:** co-locate at the top of the component file.
- **Shared types** (Commerce Cloud entities, API responses, shared hook signatures): `overrides/app/types/` — split into `commerce.ts`, `components.ts`, `hooks.ts`, re-exported via `index.ts`.
- Don't re-declare types already exported by `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` or `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` — import them directly.

## Testing

Three layers: **Vitest** (unit logic) · **Storybook** `play` (component interactions) · **Playwright** (E2E). Write tests only where failure would be non-obvious or costly to debug — data mapping, integration boundaries, complex state, and pure logic that would survive a refactor invisibly if broken. Every UI component needs a `.stories.tsx`; every logic-heavy feature needs a `.test.ts` or a story `play`.

Full layer guidance, file layout, selector priority, and mocking policy: [.claude/rules/testing.md](.claude/rules/testing.md). (The no-MSW rule in Rules applies to production paths only.)

## Graceful Degradation

Each external system must fail independently — one outage must not break the whole page. Two defaults override any per-system behaviour: **fail closed on consent** (if consent state is unknown, load no third-party scripts), and **never silently substitute a different checkout, payment, or commerce flow** when an integration is down — surface an explicit error instead.

## Performance

Mobile page speed is a top priority. Every change that touches rendering, data fetching, or assets must not regress it.

- **LCP budget is tight (≤ 2s at p75 mobile)** — Defer every third-party script that isn't required for first paint. Anything loaded via Didomi callback (GTM, Optimizely, Inside Chat, Narvar EDD, reCAPTCHA, etc.) must not block LCP — use `defer`, `async`, or post-hydration injection. If a new third-party integration looks like it might land on the critical path, flag it before merging.
- **Images:** Always use lazy loading and serve correctly sized images. Never render full-resolution images at thumbnail size.
- **Code splitting:** Prefer dynamic `import()` for heavy components not needed on initial render.
- **Data fetching:** Avoid over-fetching — request only the fields you need. Waterfall requests are not acceptable; parallelise where possible.
- **Bundle size:** Do not introduce large dependencies without confirming with the user.
- **Dependencies:** Before implementing any feature that may require a third-party library, check `package.json` for what is already installed. Evaluate whether an existing dependency can satisfy the requirement. If a better third-party option exists, present the recommendation (existing vs. new, with trade-offs) and wait for user approval before installing anything.

## Gotchas

- **Theme runtime errors:** Custom components (e.g. `ListMenu`) must be defined in the theme object or destructuring will throw.
- **Commerce SDK types not importable:** Check `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/dist/` for generated definitions, or declare a narrow local `type`.
- **Magento password migration:** Passwords were not migrated from Magento — all existing customers must reset at go-live. Do not assume any saved credentials exist. Account creation and login flows must handle this gracefully (CFD-013).

## Requirements

Requirements for this project are in `.docs/`, they must be strictly followed.
Before any code changes, verify logic against relevant `.docs/` files.
For any task that touches an external integration, check the matching `.docs/integration/NN-*.md` doc.

If a requirement is missing, ambiguous, or not yet confirmed — **stop, flag the ambiguity, propose a solution, and wait for user approval before proceeding.** Do not fill gaps with assumptions.

Verification: Start every task by briefly stating which doc/section you are following (e.g. "Implementing per auth.md section 2.1" or "Implementing per 07-adyen.md §3").

**Doc integrity:** Confirmed PRDs (`.docs/prd/`) and finalised Figma designs are the source of truth for _requirements_. `.docs/integration/` docs are guides for _how_ each integration works technically. If a user instruction contradicts either, pause immediately — cite the specific doc, section, and requirement ID — and ask the user whether the doc should be updated or the instruction is a deliberate override. Do not proceed silently either way. The same applies if you spot any improvement or conflict within the docs themselves.

## Living Memory

`.docs/memory/` is the project's persistent memory. Read [.docs/memory/projectState.md](.docs/memory/projectState.md) at the start of every session (or run `/session-start`). For what belongs in each memory file and when to update it, see the [session-start skill](.claude/skills/session-start/SKILL.md).

# Styling an Override Component

How to style a component under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/theme/`.
Cross-references [overrides.md](./overrides.md) (module-replacement correctness — a
different concern: that file is about not breaking SFCC's own imports, this one is
about what values to reach for once the component compiles). Day-to-day CSS/token
rules live in [css.md](./css.md); this file is the practical "what do I actually type"
companion.

---

## The hierarchy — reach for these in order

1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual. `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`.
   All 22 Handover text styles are registered in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`.
2. **Raw `var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom properties** for colour and spacing — `color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"`,
   `bg="var(--zimm-color-bg-02)"`, `gap="var(--zimm-scale-m)"`. **Never** a bare Chakra/theme
   token string (`color="text.default"`, `gap="m"`) — even though `theme.colors`/`theme.space`
   ARE registered from the same Zimmermann foundations (see `theme/index.ts`'s own comment on
   which scales are and aren't registered) and a bare key resolves to the identical value. This
   is a house-style requirement, not a correctness one: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference is
   unambiguous at every call site, where a bare key forces a PR reviewer to check
   `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct. Mechanically
   enforced across every recipe file by `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s "no
   override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale" test — it walks the
   registered recipe map only, so it cannot see the same mistake made as a JSX/`sx` prop (see
   that test's SCOPE note); apply the same discipline there by hand.
3. **A component's own theme config** — either centralized (`theme/components/<name>.ts`)
   or, per the co-location pattern below, beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — for
   anything that needs to vary by variant/size/state and isn't already a Chakra prop — see
   "Component-local tokens" and "Co-locating a component's theme file" below. For an
   interactive component with existing Chakra support (buttons, inputs, etc.), this theme
   config is the single source of truth — see "One canonical styling surface per component
   type" below.
4. **`sx` prop** for a one-off Chakra-prop-system gap, per [css.md](./css.md).
5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` genuinely can't express it (complex pseudo-selectors,
   keyframes) — same file, same rules as [css.md](./css.md) already documents.

**Never**: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file — reach for the token
instead. The one standing exception is `zimmButton.css.ts`'s provisional height/padding
constants (`BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y`), pending UI-designer
sign-off — see Units below. Run `npm run audit:tokens` (`node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`)
before opening a PR that touches `overrides/app/components/**` or
`overrides/app/theme/components/**` — it greps for exactly this, scoped to those two paths
(`.ts`/`.tsx`/`.scss`, excluding `*.test.ts(x)` and `*.stories.tsx`). A match is downgraded
from a failure to an acknowledged exception when the surrounding comment block already
contains `provisional`, `pending`, `placeholder`, or an explicit `audit-allow: <reason>` —
the exact vocabulary this codebase already uses for its documented raw-value exceptions, so
existing well-commented code doesn't need a second, separately-maintained allow-list. Built
2026-08-23 — it is not wired into CI yet, deliberately: someone still needs to own triaging a
full run's worth of pre-existing findings first (a first run against this repo surfaced 14
genuine pre-existing violations, none touched by that session, all outside its scope to fix).
Note this is a *different, broader* check than `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token-key guard
mentioned above: that one exists and runs today (`npm run test`), but only catches a bare
Chakra key standing in for a zimm var — it says nothing about a raw hex/px/rem/em literal,
which is what `audit:tokens` is for.

## Units

- **`rem`** for anything that should scale with the user's root font-size / browser zoom
  (WCAG 1.4.4): type (`fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`) and spacing
  (`spacing.ts`'s named scale). Letter-spacing values that were specified as sub-pixel px
  in the source don't round to clean rem numbers, so those keep a trailing `// -0.12px`
  comment for traceability.
- **`px`** for hairline geometry that should _not_ scale: border widths, focus-ring
  offsets, and (for now) the provisional button-height constants in `zimmButton.css.ts` that are
  still pending UI-designer sign-off against Handover.
- **`em`** only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts` — deliberate, so `.zimm-grid`'s media
  queries shift with zoom the same way Chakra's responsive props do) and other
  genuinely context-relative cases. Not a general-purpose unit.

## The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy

`theme/foundation/colour.ts`'s primitive tier (`grey`, `ivory`, ...) is defined first as
plain `const`s, and the semantic/alias tier below it (`text`, `background`, `border`,
...) reads from those consts (`text.default: grey[900]`) instead of retyping the hex
value. Do the same for any new primitive/alias pair you add — two values can't disagree
if only one of them is ever typed.

`zimmTokens.ts` (the `--zimm-*` CSS-var registry for `globalStyles.ts`'s `.zimm-*`
classes) is fully derived the same way — it imports `colors`/`spacing`/`fontSizes`/
`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/`fontWeights`/`iconSizes`/`actionSizes`/`motion`/`grid`
from their owning files rather than retyping values. The only literals left are the 7
numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases with no named-scale equivalent (`025`, `700`, `1100`,
`1200`, `1300`, `3500`, `4500`) — not duplicates, just Handover values with nothing to
derive them from. `theme/index.test.tsx`'s collision-guard tests still exist as a
regression net; treat a failure there as a real drift signal, not test noise.

## One canonical styling surface per component type

Only one place should define how a given interactive component looks: its theme config —
either centralized as `theme/components/<name>.ts` or, per the co-location pattern below,
beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — consumed via Chakra's component (`<Button>`,
`<Link>` variant, etc.). Don't also give it a `.zimm-*` global class in
`globalStyles.ts` — a static CSS class can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/
`_focusVisible` states the way a Chakra theme config can, so a class "mirror" is
structurally incomplete from the start, and nothing stops its values from disagreeing
with the real theme config over time. `zimmButton.css.ts` (co-located at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/`) is the single source of truth for
button styling; `globalStyles.ts` has no `.zimm-btn-*` classes — use Chakra's `<Button>`
for any button, not a class.

`.zimm-*` classes remain the right tool for genuinely static, non-interactive,
massively-reused treatments (typography, the responsive grid, form-field layout) where
there's no interactive state to lose.

## Importing an already-overridden component from a new component

If component A (e.g. `productDetailOptions`) uses component B, and B already has an
override (e.g. `swatch-group`), **import B via a relative path
(`'../swatch-group'`), not the SFCC base path
(`'@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group'`)** — even though the
base path is exactly what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) requires _inside_ an override
that's itself shadowing an SFCC module (see `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
import, which is correct for that file).

The reason the two cases differ: the resolver that redirects
`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports to `overrides/` (`ccExtensibility` in
`package.json`, read by a webpack plugin) only runs in the **real app build** — dev
server and production. `.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to
`node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` doesn't touch it at all, so neither loads the
resolver. A base-path import of an already-overridden component will build and run
correctly in the shipped app, but silently render/test the **unstyled base SFCC
version** in Storybook and Vitest — the story or test looks like it's exercising your
override and isn't.

**Known instance of this, not yet fixed:** `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
import uses the base path. Currently dormant only because its Storybook story exercises
the `CardBaseline` named export (which takes `price` as a pre-rendered node and never
calls `DisplayPrice`), not the default `ProductTile` bridge that actually renders it —
worth fixing before anything writes a story/test against the default export.

An override component's own base-path imports (of modules it is _not_ also
overriding) are unaffected by this — `RecommendedProducts`, `Seo`, `QuantityPicker`
etc. have no local override to miss, so the base path is simply correct for them.

## Component-local tokens

When a component needs a spacing/sizing value that already has a `spacing.ts` /
`iconSizes` / etc. entry, reference that entry **as a `var(--zimm-*)` custom property**
— `marginBottom: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)'`, not `marginBottom: 2`, not
`marginBottom: '0.5rem'`, and **not** the bare key `marginBottom: 'xs'`. The bare-key
form resolved correctly against the registered `theme.space` and was what this section
used to recommend, but hierarchy point 2 above now forbids it and
`theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token guard **fails the build on it** —
so following the old advice inside a registered recipe breaks `npm run test`.

See `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts` and
`.../footer/bottomBar/bottomBar.css.ts` for the pattern in a real recipe. The reason is
traceability, not parity with the base theme: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference names the
Figma token it came from, where a raw `2` or `'0.5rem'` names nothing. (Note these
recipes are deliberately namespaced `ZimmFooter*` so they do **not** inherit the base
SFCC `Footer` config — their values come from Figma, not from re-expressing base
numerics. See `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s namespacing guard.)

**Responsive steps are explicit media queries, not Chakra's array shorthand.** A
co-located recipe keys them off `BP` in `theme/components/footerShared.ts`, in the form:

```ts
[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)' },
```

The array shorthand (`['2xs', '2xs', 'xs', 'xs']`) is what this section used to
recommend, and it would put a bare token key back at every step — the guard walks
responsive arrays and attributes each element to the same prop, so all four fail.
`footer.css.ts`'s `contentRow` and `linksInner` parts are the reference.

When a component needs a dimension with **no existing foundation entry** (and you don't
have a confirmed Figma value for it), leave it inherited from the base SFCC theme rather
than inventing a number — don't guess at design values. Follow the precedent already in
`header.ts`/`zimmButton.css.ts`: if you do have to ship a placeholder value pending designer
sign-off, say so in a comment next to it, the same way those files already do.

## The SFCC bridge pattern (shared components only)

If the component is used internally by SFCC's own base components (check with `grep -r
"from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'"
node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`), its **default export must stay a
faithful, undecorated port** — full original prop surface, same `forwardRef` behaviour,
matching what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) already requires for correctness. Put
Zimmermann-only styling behind a **named export** that wraps the default and adds
brand-specific defaults, the same split `product-tile/index.tsx` (`CardBaseline`
name + default) and `link/index.tsx` already use. `image-gallery`, `display-price`, and
`swatch-group` are all shared internal SFCC dependencies. When one of them does get
overridden, keep its default export API-compatible and put brand styling in a theme

# CSS & Styling Conventions

Chakra UI and `.scss` conventions. See [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Rules > Styling for the
higher-level policy (Chakra props first, `.scss` only when insufficient, theme file
ownership/tiers) — this file covers the concrete day-to-day rules underneath that policy.

---

## Tokens — no hardcoded design values

Chakra UI props must use the Chakra token system — no hardcoded hex colours, no pixel
values for spacing, no raw font sizes. Tokens belong in
[overrides/app/theme/foundation/](../../overrides/app/theme/) (Tier 1 — see
[frozenFiles.md](./frozenFiles.md)).

```tsx
// ❌ hardcoded
<Box color="#1A1A1A" padding="16px" />

// ❌ a bare Chakra/theme token string — resolves correctly (theme.colors/theme.space ARE
// registered from the Zimmermann foundations) but is still not allowed in an override
// component; see overrideStyling.md's hierarchy point 2 for why
<Box color="text.default" padding="m" />

// ✅ token, as a raw var(--zimm-*) reference
<Box color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)" padding="var(--zimm-scale-m)" />
```

Type is its own case, not shown above — set it with `textStyle` (`textStyle="body2"`), never
a raw `fontSize`, per [overrideStyling.md](./overrideStyling.md) point 1. There's no
`var(--zimm-*)` substitute for the composite `textStyle` expansion itself, only for its
individual pieces (`var(--zimm-font-size-*)` etc.), so `textStyle` stays a bare key —
it's the one entry in the hierarchy that isn't a colour/spacing token.

**The raw-hex/px/rem/em half of this has a script but no CI gate yet.**
`npm run audit:tokens` (`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`) scans `overrides/app/components/**`
and `overrides/app/theme/components/**` for exactly this — see
[overrideStyling.md](./overrideStyling.md)'s `Never` note for the full scope and its
acknowledged-exception rules. It's not wired into CI (no `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/` rule
either), so nothing blocks a merge that skips running it — that's still a real gap, just not
an unstarted one.
The bare-token-vs-`var(--zimm-*)` half above **is** mechanically enforced for recipe files —
see `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`, which runs on every `npm run test` — though it
can't see the same mistake made as a JSX/`sx` prop; that half still relies on review.

---

## `.scss` — only when Chakra props are insufficient

Per AGENTS.md, reach for a `.scss` file alongside a component only when Chakra's prop system
genuinely can't express what's needed (e.g. complex pseudo-selectors, keyframe animations,
print styles). When you do:

- **File naming:** matches the component file exactly — `productTile.scss` next to
  `productTile/index.tsx` (see [conventions.md](./conventions.md) > File naming and folder
  structure for the folder layout this sits in).
- **Scoped, co-located only.** No global stylesheets outside `overrides/app/theme/` — a
  component's `.scss` file must only affect that component's own markup.
- **Nesting depth ≤ 3 levels.** Beyond that, the selector is almost always reaching into a
  child component's internals rather than styling its own root — a sign the styling belongs
  in that child instead, or that Chakra's `sx` prop / a theme variant would express it more
  directly.
- **No ID selectors.** Class-based only — an ID selector's specificity makes it
  disproportionately hard to override later (including by a legitimate future Chakra
  variant), and IDs aren't guaranteed unique when a component renders more than once on a
  page.
- **No `!important`** without an inline comment explaining why the override is genuinely
  unavoidable (e.g. fighting a third-party widget's inline styles) — same reasoning as the
  `any`/non-null-assertion escape hatches in [typescript.md](./typescript.md): allowed, but
  the reason has to be visible at the point of use, not left for the next reader to guess.
- **Prefer Chakra's `sx` prop or a theme variant extension over a new `.scss` file** for
  anything that's really just "a Chakra style the prop system doesn't have a named prop for"
  — a new global class is a bigger footprint than a one-off `sx` override, and `sx` keeps the
  style co-located with the JSX that uses it instead of a separate file to keep in sync.

# Code Conventions

Cross-cutting code-writing rules that apply to every file in a PR, regardless of type. Domain-specific
conventions are split into their own files — see **See also** below. Both
[.claude/skills/new-component/](../skills/new-component/SKILL.md) (when scaffolding) and
[.claude/skills/code-quality/](../skills/code-quality/SKILL.md) (when auditing) reference this
file and its siblings. Update the relevant file once — both skills, and (via
[scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs](../../scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs)) all other AI tool configs,
pick it up.

> Higher-level project rules live in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md). Tier classifications live in
> [frozenFiles.md](./frozenFiles.md) and [protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md).

## See also

- **[typescript.md](./typescript.md)** — TypeScript idioms: `any`/`type` vs `interface`,
  discriminated unions, utility types, `satisfies`, `readonly`, generics.
- **[css.md](./css.md)** — Chakra token usage, hardcoded-value policy, `.scss` conventions.
- **[components.md](./components.md)** — component/hook/Storybook structure and the
  composition rules for a "clean" component (complexity limits, container/presentational
  separation, extract-to-hook threshold).
- **[testing.md](./testing.md)** — Vitest / Storybook `play` / Playwright layer selection.
- **[frozenFiles.md](./frozenFiles.md)** / **[protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md)** —
  Tier 1 / Tier 2 file protection.

---

## General — every file in a PR

These apply to all `.ts`/`.tsx` files Claude creates or modifies, regardless of folder.

- **TypeScript only inside `overrides/`.** `.js`/`.jsx` is not acceptable here — see AGENTS.md.
- **No commented-out code blocks introduced by this PR** unless accompanied by an explicit
  strong reason in a comment immediately above. Existing comments are preserved per AGENTS.md —
  the rule is about _introducing_ new dead code, not removing old.
- **No `console.log` or `console.error` calls** outside of error boundaries or explicit
  developer-tooling files. Use the project's logger when one is introduced.
- **No hardcoded design values** — Chakra token usage is a whole topic of its own now; see
  [css.md](./css.md).
- **React rules of hooks apply everywhere hooks are called.** Only call hooks at the top
  level of a component or another hook. No conditional, looped, or nested hook calls.
- **TypeScript idioms** (`any`, `type` vs `interface`, and the rest) — see
  [typescript.md](./typescript.md).
- **Australian spelling** in Zimmermann-authored identifiers and copy (`colour`, `centre`,
  `organisation`). Override files keep upstream Salesforce spelling verbatim.
- **Apply DRY, KISS, and SOLID.** Don't repeat logic — extract to a shared utility or hook
  once the same pattern appears in two places. Prefer the simplest design that works; resist
  speculative abstractions. Keep modules to a single responsibility; split a file when it
  starts mixing concerns.
- **No magic numbers or strings.** Any literal value with semantic meaning — pixel
  thresholds, retry counts, country codes, feature flag names, status strings, error
  codes — must be a named constant (`const MAX_RETRIES = 3`) or live in a config/enum
  module. Excepted: `0`, `1`, `-1` in obvious idiomatic uses, and string literals that _are_
  the value (e.g. CSS class names, JSX text).
- **Payment credentials — never logged, never persisted client-side.** Gift card numbers,
  gift card PINs, credit card PANs, CVVs and similar secrets must not appear in any
  `console.*` call, Sentry breadcrumb / event, GTM dataLayer push, analytics event, MRT
  access log, or response body returned to the browser beyond a masked form. Never store
  them in `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, IndexedDB, or cookies — form state lives in
  React only and is cleared on unmount. Submit them in the POST **body**, never as a
  query string (URLs end up in MRT access logs, browser history, Referer headers). After
  submit, render only the serial portion (e.g. `••••••••1234`). Do not add body-logging
  middleware on routes that carry these fields. Logger and Sentry `beforeSend` must
  redact them. See [.docs/prd/giftcards.md §10](../../.docs/prd/giftcards.md) for the
  GiveX-specific rationale (only the card's serial portion may be displayed or logged).
- **`dangerouslySetInnerHTML` must always wrap its value in a sanitizer call**
  (e.g. `DOMPurify.sanitize(...)`) — never pass raw/unsanitized HTML (CMS content,
  API responses, user input). Unsanitized HTML injection is an XSS vector. Enforced
  by a `semgrep.yml` rule at PR review time — get it right at authoring time instead
  of finding out post-review.

---

## File naming and folder structure

- **Zimmermann-authored files and folders:** `camelCase` (e.g. `productTile.tsx`,
  `useWishlist.ts`, `formatPrice.ts`).
- **Override files (mirroring a base Salesforce file):** keep the original kebab-case
  filename and folder name exactly (e.g. `product-tile.tsx`). This makes the origin of a
  file obvious at a glance.
- **Component folder layout:** each component lives in its own folder under
  [overrides/app/components/](../../overrides/app/components/). Use `index.tsx` for the
  component itself so imports stay clean:

  ```
  overrides/app/components/productTile/
    index.tsx              ← the component
    index.stories.tsx      ← Storybook story
    index.test.ts          ← Vitest (only if logic-heavy)
    types.ts               ← only if props/types are shared with sibling files
    productTile.scss       ← only if Chakra props are insufficient
  ```

  Import as `import ProductTile from '.../components/productTile'`.

---

## Utilities

- **Pure functions** — no side effects unless clearly intentional and called out in a comment.
- **No imports from `overrides/app/hooks/`** — utilities must not depend on hooks
  (it's the other direction).
- **Vitest required** when the utility has ≥1 conditional branch or performs ≥1
  transformation (currency, locale, mapping, parsing, etc.). Trivial re-exports or
  one-liners don't need a test.

---

## Imports

- **No circular imports** — if file A imports from file B, B must not import from A
  (check one level deep).
- **No `../../../..` chains longer than 3 levels** — flag for path-alias review.
- **No imports from internal `node_modules/@salesforce/...` source paths** — use the
  package's published entrypoints (`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...`).
- **No imports from a later-sprint feature** — cross-check
  `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`.
