386	6. Live verification is **deferred** per §7 — the code is in scope, the defect ticket and the live proof are not. Say so in the PR body so nobody reads the merge as verified.
387	
388	#### Step 4.2 — `useCartMergeAndCap`
389	
390	**Changes.** One shared function called by both the post-auth callback and the render guard — one implementation, not two copies.
391	
392	Settled shape, all of it: threshold **`>=`** not `==` (a line already holding 4 must fail the check, or the `+` stays live exactly when it matters); scope is **per line item**, not per SKU (the SKU is already size + colour, so in normal shopping one line is one SKU); cap **consolidates to one line at 3** (free — `sum_quantities` already produces a single merged line item); callback order **merge → cap → 272's wishlist resume** (the wishlist move acts on a line the merge may have just consolidated and the cap just reduced; reversing it moves a quantity the shopper never saw); render guard is a secondary backstop that **no-ops while `useIsMutating()` is non-zero**, so it cannot race the callback; **keep the loop guard** — one correction in flight, one attempt per basket version, then stop and surface an error, because a write-on-render without it can rate-limit a shopper out of their own basket; **no action on the brief 4-then-3 flash** — observe real behaviour first.
393	
394	**Pass criteria.**
395	1. Unit tests: line at 2 with max 3 → no change. Line at 3 → no change (`>=` boundary, the case `==` gets wrong is 4). Line at 4 → reduced to 3. Line at 5 → reduced to 3. Two lines of the same SKU at 2 each after a `sum_quantities` merge → one consolidated line at 3.
396	2. `useIsMutating()` non-zero → function returns without issuing a write. Asserted, not assumed.
397	3. Loop guard: two consecutive invocations against the **same** basket version issue exactly **one** write. A server rejection surfaces an error and does **not** retry indefinitely.
398	4. Callback order asserted: with all three armed, merge resolves before cap, and cap resolves before the wishlist resume. Assert on call order, not on final state — final state can look right with the wrong order.
399	5. Max value comes from `maxOrderQuantity.ts` (step 3.4), not a literal.
400	6. **State in the PR body that this is not end-to-end verifiable** until SFCC-268's `afterGET` hook is deployed (gate findings #1/#2 — the TSD is `v0.1 Draft`, Technical Lead sign-off Pending, and the live dev-sandbox probe found no `c_maxOrderQuantity` on any product, while Jira has 268 as Ready for SIT). The fallback path is what is being tested.
401	
402	#### Step 4.3 — `useCartMessages`: one handler, one file to swap
403	
404	**Changes.** Every message — success, error, warning — is emitted through **one** function, so SFCC-404 is later a renderer swap in a single file. A marker comment naming SFCC-404 sits at the emit site.
405	
406	Interim surface is the base Chakra toast. **See open question 4 before writing the import line** — `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts` does not exist, and creating it is a Tier 2 change this bundle has not budgeted for.
407	
408	Copy (Figma leading, per the cards): single message uses the **product-named** variant, "Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist"; already-in-wishlist is "An item in your bag already exists in Wishlist"; max-reached is "An item in your bag has reached maximum quantity". The generic stacked variant ("Item added to Wishlist") is only reachable once 404 lands with real stacking — a toast has no aggregation concept and is always on its own from the shopper's point of view, so the **interim toast uses the product-named copy**. Both divergences from SFCC-272's AC wording go on the deferred Jira comment; the cards are not edited.
409	
410	**Pass criteria.**
411	1. `grep -rn "useToast\|toast(" overrides/app/pages/cart overrides/app/components/ui-kits/**/zimmCart*` shows exactly **one** emit site.
412	2. Each of the three copy strings is asserted verbatim in a test.
413	3. A Storybook `play` asserting a message queries `within(document.body)` with an inline comment citing `testing.md`'s portal exception — Chakra toasts portal outside `canvasElement` and this is the only sanctioned use of `within(document.body)`.
414	4. The SFCC-404 marker comment is present and names the ticket.
415	
416	#### Step 4.4 — `ZimmCartItemActions` + pending-item-across-auth
417	
418	**Changes.** Remove / Move to Wishlist as **underlined text links below the stepper** (SFCC-270 AC8, styled in B3's pass). Gap **24px**, not Figma's raw 25px — §11.10(4), snapped to the nearest tokenised value with a comment saying the design specified 25. Links `capitalize`, `textStyle="linkSm"`, `link/default` → `--zimm-color-text-default`.
419	
420	Note the actions are **not** inside base `product-item` — it receives them as a `secondaryActions` prop from its caller. So this molecule is supplied by the container, and we do not fight the base structure to inject it.
421	
422	Remove: item removed, drawer count decrements, totals update; quantity > 1 removes all units in one action.
423	
424	Wishlist, guest: the existing `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` via `useWishlistAuthDrawer`, **one hook instance**, `intentId: 'cart-wishlist'`. Per gate #5, this is a **deliberate override** of two sources that say "login page" (SFCC-272 AC7 and Confluence CAI-018), justified by consistency with the four other auth-drawer surfaces — record it as an override, not as an AC reading. The `.docs/prd/cart.md` §2 paraphrase is the weaker justification and should not be the one cited.
425	
426	Pending item held in **React state** (covers email-code and create-account, where the page never unloads) **and** session storage (covers the Apple/Google redirect). Read state first, fall back to storage, clear **both** together. Same **5-minute** age bound as the hook's own intent (`PENDING_WISHLIST_INTENT_MAX_AGE_MS`), so a stale item cannot be resumed.
427	
428	Rejected and not to be revisited: one hook instance per line item (mounts a `useForm`, three `useAuthHelper`s, a `useAuthModal` and a drawer **per row** — a ten-item bag mounts ten of each, against a stated mobile-page-speed priority); adding an optional `itemId` to the shared `PendingWishlistIntent` (better long-term, but changes a shared hook with three existing call sites — raise separately).
429	
430	**Pass criteria — both links are interactive controls, so every state is named:**
431	1. Default: underlined, capitalized, `--zimm-color-text-default`, 24px gap, height 24 / py 4.
432	2. **Hover, focus-visible, active** inherited from `ZimmLink`'s recipe. Assert the focus-visible ring is **not identical** to default. Figma supplies only the `link/default` token for these links; inheritance is the resolution, annotated. If `ZimmLink` turns out to carry no focus treatment, that is an open question at that moment — not something to leave for the Tester.
433	3. Disabled: **not specified in Figma for these links and not required by any AC.** Do not build one.
434	4. Remove with quantity 1 → one `removeItemFromBasket` call, count decrements by 1.
435	5. Remove with quantity 3 → **one** call, count decrements by 3 (AC3 — all units in one action, not three calls).
436	6. Authenticated wishlist move, quantity 3 → all units removed from cart, **a single SKU saved** to wishlist, count decrements by 3, product-named success message emitted (AC5).
437	7. Already in wishlist → warning-variant message with the exact Figma copy, **item remains in cart** (AC6).
438	8. Guest click → auth drawer opens, **item stays in cart** (AC7).
439	9. Guest completes email-code auth → pending item resumes from React state, moves, success message. Then a separate test: pending item resumes from **session storage** after a simulated redirect.
440	10. A pending item older than 5 minutes is **not** resumed, and both state and storage are cleared.
441	11. Resume fires **after** merge and cap (asserted in step 4.2's order test).
442	
443	#### Step 4.5 — `ZimmCartEmptyState`
444	
445	**Changes.** A **discrete component, not inline JSX in the drawer**, so SFCC-277 is a swap in one file. Structure from the `recentlyViewed/index.tsx` precedent (`Box > Center > Stack`, `isRegistered`-branched copy, `Button as={Link}` using the **base SFCC `Link`** so the CTA href gets multi-site prefixing via `use-multi-site`'s `buildUrl`, `useIntl` in the leaf under the Context exception, decision log at the bottom of the file). Visuals from SFCC-315's EMPTY BAG Figma nodes, not from that precedent's autonomous token choices.
446	
447	Layout per §11.7: two columns collapse to one, Cart-item-group → 360×157, Totals summary moves x=500 → x=0 and shrinks 430×857 → 430×263. Paragraph spacing **24px**, not the design's raw 25px, with the same snapping comment.
448	
449	**Ship a placeholder body only.** Marcel settled that the hardcoded AU Client Services phone/hours/email are not this build's problem — SFCC-277 owns the real empty state, and the per-storefront question carries to 277's grooming.
450	
451	**Pass criteria.**
452	1. Renders as its own component, imported by the drawer. `grep` confirms no inline empty-state JSX in `zimmCartDrawer/index.tsx`.
453	2. Removing the last item shows it (AC2), and the drawer header simultaneously reads `YOUR BAG IS EMPTY`.
454	3. CTA uses the base SFCC `Link`, and a test at a non-AU site asserts the href carries the site prefix.
455	4. Two-to-one column collapse asserted in the recipe test.
456	5. No AU phone number, hours string or email hardcoded in the shipped placeholder.
457	
458	---
459	
460	### B5 — SFCC-275, button group
461	
462	#### Step 5.1 — `ZimmCartButtonGroup`
463	
464	**Changes.** New molecule: `flex-col`, gap **16px**, all buttons **h52 / px32 / min-w 80 / w-full**. Checkout = `ZimmButton` `primary` (bg `--zimm-color-...` from `grey[900]`, white text, **UPPERCASE**, `textStyle="button"`). Apple Pay and Google Pay = `ZimmButton` `secondary` (1px border, same grey[900]), logos 48×24 as **button children** — their absolute positioning in Figma is a compositional shortcut, not a layout instruction.
465	
466	h52 == `actionSizes.height.lg`, px32 == `paddingX.lg`, gap16 == `actionSizes.gap`. **No atom gap** — verified. Reference the existing tokens; do not type the numbers.
467	
468	Fixed order, always: Checkout → Apple Pay → Google Pay (AC1).
469	
470	International: express buttons **removed, not hidden** — the Figma Button-group has exactly one child. AC2's "no white gap" is therefore a plain conditional render with nothing to compensate for. Branch on `checkoutOwner` from `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` via `overrides/app/hooks/useCountryConfig.ts` — that field's own doc comment directs exactly this use ("Branch checkout AND pricing logic from this field at PDP/cart level — not only at the checkout page"). Read the config; **do not modify `countries.ts`** (Tier 1).
471	
472	Check `useExpressCheckoutEnabled()` — base `cart-cta.jsx` already gates express buttons — before writing new show/hide logic.
473	
474	ACs 3/4: buttons render **visually enabled** during error states. Backend blocking is not in a UI story, and the ACs specify no shopper-facing feedback for a click that does nothing. Per gate #3, CAI-035's "disable the Checkout CTA" reconciles with AC3 only if the block fires on the checkout *attempt* rather than pre-emptively in the cart — carry that as the stated assumption. Flag the feedback gap in the PR body; **do not invent copy**.
475	
476	ACs 6/7: build the branch, **stub the destination**. SFCC-880 is To Do, unassigned, no sprint; Global-e is Not started. Leaving international on the base `/checkout` path is the current behaviour, so the stub is a no-op, not a regression.
477	
478	**Pass criteria — three interactive controls, every state named:**
479	1. Domestic: exactly three children in the documented order.
480	2. International: exactly **one** child in the DOM. Assert `queryByRole('button', {name: /apple pay/i})` is `null` — not merely `not.toBeVisible()`. And assert the group's resolved height is unchanged, proving no compensating gap was added.
481	3. Checkout button: **default** (grey[900] bg, white text, uppercase, h52/px32/gap16 asserted against the `actionSizes` tokens), **hover**, **focus-visible**, **active**, **disabled** — all four non-default states inherited from `ZimmButton`'s `primary` variant, with an assertion that focus-visible differs from default. Figma supplies only the `action/primary/bg/default` token; the Design System 2026 file was not opened (gate #17), so inheritance from our already-reconciled atom is the resolution, annotated.
482	4. Apple Pay and Google Pay: same five states from `ZimmButton` `secondary`.
483	5. Error-in-cart story: all three render **enabled**, and no feedback copy exists anywhere in the component.
484	6. Domestic, both auth states → Checkout navigates to `/checkout`. International guest and international authenticated → the branch is taken and hits the stub; a test asserts the stub is reached and names SFCC-880 / SFCC-63 in a comment.
485	7. `git status` shows `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` unmodified.
486	8. Story `title` is `'Commerce/ZimmCartButtonGroup'`.
487	9. **Blocked sub-item:** see open question 6 — the Apple Pay and Google Pay marks do not exist in `overrides/app/components/icons/`. AC1 cannot fully pass until they do.
488

# Cart bundle (SFCC-11) — executable build plan

## 1. Goal statement

Build the Zimmermann cart drawer and its line-item system — SFCC-315, 270, 795, 271, 272, 250, 275 — as prescribed by those seven Sprint 5 cards, as designed in Figma file `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` nodes `9323-65888/65895/65983/66104` (DEFAULT PAGE TEMPLATE) plus the CART MERGE, WISHLIST, INTERNATIONAL, EMPTY BAG and OOS state groups across all four breakpoints, as approached by the FED handbook and `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, as established in PR #85 (SFCC-236 shared product card — atoms → molecules → organism, page-level mapper, `ui-kits/<name>Shared.ts`, theme registration, `desktop/`/`mobile/` e2e split), using: the **override** approach with copy-first for `product-item/` and `item-variant/` (mirrored base files exist), the **new-component** approach under `ui-kits/` for the drawer organism, quantity stepper, inline message, actions row, button group and empty state (no mirrored base file exists), **co-located `Zimm*` recipes** for all styling, and the **existing `--zimm-*` foundation untouched** — every colour and space value in this design already exists there.

---

## 2. Scale call — six branches, and how much loop each earns

> **⚠️ SUPERSEDED by §11 (Marcel, 2026-09-17): SINGLE PR, now 20 commits** (18 originally; the
> 3.5 stepper-wiring insertion on 2026-09-18 made it 19, the 4.6 cartDrawerContainer insertion on
> 2026-09-20 made it 20 — this line and the other plain "18"/"eighteen" mentions below went stale
> both times and were only just corrected; treat this number as the one to keep current, not
> re-derive from memory, if a further step ever gets inserted).
> Retained as the record of why the seams were drawn where they were. §3's file manifest and §4's
> steps remain valid verbatim — they regroup by commit instead of by branch. §5's per-step loop
> criteria remain valid; only the per-*branch* loop scaling is replaced.

### Six branches, not one PR and not seven

| # | Branch | Stories | Files | Why it is its own branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **B0** | `fix/SFCC-11_cart-e2e-area` | — (infra) | 1 | `.github/workflows/qa.yml` is **Tier 1 CI/CD**. Bundling it into a feature PR drags `@tier-1-approvers` onto a feature review and breaches AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 (one protection tier per change). |
| **B1** | `feature/SFCC-315_cart-drawer` | 315 | ~7 | **Ships first and standalone.** SFCC-316 (Jhoan, same sprint, Ready for Development) composes into it. Anything that delays this branch delays someone else's active-sprint card. |
| **B2** | `feature/SFCC-270_cart-item-override` | 270 | ~14 | **The only Tier 2 code branch.** `product-item/` pulls `@pwa-squad-b @tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. Keeping it alone means one squad-B reviewer sees one coherent override, not a 40-file cart feature. Also the only branch with a mandatory copy-first pause. |
| **B3** | `feature/SFCC-795-271_cart-item-states-stepper` | 795 + 271 | ~20 | 795 and 271 are the same pixels. §5.4: "795 subsumes 270, 271 and 250's UI states — one implementation, three cards' ACs." Splitting them means building the stepper twice. |
| **B4** | `feature/SFCC-250-272_max-qty-wishlist-actions` | 250 + 272 | ~16 | **Welded, per the settled decision.** Both land in one `onAuthSuccess` callback (merge → cap → wishlist resume). They cannot be reviewed or reverted independently. |
| **B5** | `feature/SFCC-275_cart-button-group` | 275 | ~6 | Independent of the cart-item chain. Can run in parallel with B2/B3 by a second pair of hands. |

Every branch is cut fresh from an updated `develop` (`origin/develop` head `71025f18`; local is 41 behind). Never from `feature/SFCC-831-689_country-language-mismatch`, which carries open PR #112.

**Order:** B0 ∥ B1 first → B2 (copy-first pause) → B3 → B4. B5 any time after B0. B4 depends on B3's stepper existing and on B1's drawer hosting the empty state.

### One Tier 2 touch you cannot design away

Every branch that adds a recipe must edit `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` to register it. That file is inside `overrides/app/theme/components/` → **Tier 2**, `@tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. The co-location relief in CODEOWNERS (`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → squads only, last-match-wins) covers the recipe *file* and not the registration *line*. So B1, B3, B4 and B5 each carry one Tier 2 approver for a one-line import + one key. Plan for it; do not be surprised by it at PR time.

### How much loop — scaled down deliberately

| Branch | Loop | Why |
|---|---|---|
| B0 | **None.** | A workflow allow-list. Verified by observing the next cart PR's `e2e_scope` output, not by a Tester. A loop here is theatre. |
| B1 | **Light** — Tester + Scorer on one pass. | Mostly reuse: `ZimmDrawer` already owns overlay, right placement, Escape, `finalFocusRef`, mobile full-height and scroll-lock. Two things are genuinely new (the 52px reserved band, the `xLarge` width fix) and both are assertable in one `.css.test.ts`. |
| B2 | **Full loop, but only on the copy-first pass.** | The risk here is not "does it look right", it is "did the override intercept and did the 11 downstream surfaces survive". After Marcel's verification the restyle is conventional. Dropping the second loop pass. |
| B3 | **Full loop.** | Largest surface: ~25 ACs including 11 accessibility, five stepper states, three error states, two breakpoint reflows. This is where a missed state ships. |
| B4 | **Full loop, and the only step that gets a second adversarial pass.** | Async state, an auth seam, an ordered callback, a loop guard and a render guard that must not race a mutation. Highest defect cost, lowest visibility in review. |
| B5 | **Light.** | 8 ACs, six presentational, one conditional render, one stubbed destination. A two-point story does not earn a full loop. |

**Explicitly dropped, and why:** no Playwright spec on B1 (nothing to drive it — see open question 7); no `.test.ts` on the four pure-presentation atoms/molecules whose only logic is prop interpolation (`testing.md`'s single-parent exemption — covered by the organism's `play`); no separate loop pass on B2's restyle commit. Anything more would be over-scaled machinery, which is a defect in a plan.

### B1 — SFCC-315, cart drawer organism

#### Step 1.1 — Fix `ZimmDrawer`'s `xLarge` width (this is a real bug, not a tidy-up)

**Consequence first.** `zimmDrawer.css.ts` already ships an `xLarge` size whose own comment says it is for Cart. Its value is `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'`. Figma's cart panel is a **fixed 1186px** at both 1440 and 1920 (§11.1; panel `x=256` on the 1440 frame and `x=736` on the 1920 frame — 1184 both times, so the *gap* grows and the panel does not). 82% of 1920 is **1574px** — 388px wider than designed. The inner composition is itself fixed (128 + 360 + 140 + 430 + 128 = 1186), so on a 1920 screen the shopper gets 388px of dead white space inside the panel, and the two-column layout sits off-centre. Build SFCC-315 on the existing variant unchanged and it is wrong on every large monitor.

**Mechanism.** The 82% came from a Figma frame annotation, and `zimmDrawer.css.ts`'s own comment records that the *previous* reading of that same annotation was already wrong once ("that frame's annotation was wrong (or superseded)"). The annotation is a percentage; the frames are a fixed width.

**Changes.** Replace `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'` with a rem constant equal to 1186px (`74.125rem`), applied as `width`/`maxWidth` with `maxWidth: '100%'` so it cannot exceed a narrow viewport. Keep the comment convention: cite the Figma frames, state that 82% was the annotation and 1186 is the measurement, per the `zimmButton.css.ts` house pattern.

**Pass criteria.**
1. `zimmDrawer.css.test.ts` gains an assertion that `xLarge.content` resolves to the 1186px rem value above `md`, and that `maxWidth` is `100%`.
2. No other size variant's resolved output changes — assert `large`, `tablet`, `small`, `prompt`, `mobile` snapshots are byte-identical to before.
3. `grep -rn "xLarge" overrides/app --include="*.tsx"` returns only `index.tsx`'s type union and `index.stories.tsx` — **confirmed zero production consumers today**, so blast radius is nil. Re-run this before committing; if a consumer has appeared, stop.
4. `npm run audit:tokens` does not flag the new rem constant (it carries a `// audit-allow:` or `provisional` comment naming the Figma frame, matching `PANEL_MIN_NARROW`'s existing treatment in the same file).

### B4 — SFCC-250 + 272

#### Step 4.1 — The merge call (must come first)

**Consequence first.** Today, passwordless OTP sign-in from the wishlist auth drawer does **not** merge baskets. SLAS switches the session to the registered customer and the guest basket is **orphaned — the shopper's items are gone, not miscounted.** Until this is fixed, SFCC-250's AC5 has nothing to cap and SFCC-272's AC8 has no cart item left to move. It is step one of B4 by necessity, not by preference.

**Mechanism.** Base `use-auth-modal.js` pairs its own passwordless flow with a `mergeBasket` call. `useWishlistAuthDrawer` reimplemented passwordless login for the drawer and did not carry the merge across. The social-IDP route is fine (it redirects through base `social-login-redirect`, which merges); create-account correctly skips (a new customer has no prior basket). Only `LoginPasswordlessUser` is affected. `grep -rn "mergeBasket" overrides/` is empty — no Zimmermann code merges anything.

**Changes.** Add a Zimmermann-owned `mergeBasket` call in `overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`, with `productItemMergeMode: 'sum_quantities'` and `createDestinationBasket: true`.

**Corrected 2026-09-19, before this step's Implementer was dispatched — the exact call site above was wrong, found by reading base's real mechanism instead of this paragraph's own original summary of it.** This originally said "at the point `loginPasswordless.mutateAsync` succeeds... around line 230" (i.e., inside `handleOtpVerification`). Base's own `use-auth-modal.js` does **not** call `handleMergeBasket` from its own equivalent of `handleOtpVerification` at all — it calls it from a separate `useEffect(() => {...}, [isRegistered])` that fires once the customer's registered state actually flips true, paired with `onLoginSuccess()`. `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` already has the exact structural equivalent of that effect (its own `isRegistered` effect that calls `onClose()`/`onAuthSuccess?.()`) — the merge call belongs there, alongside `onAuthSuccess?.()`, not inside `handleOtpVerification`. Reasoning: `loginPasswordless.mutateAsync` resolving only means the SDK set the session; `isRegistered` (derived from `useCustomerType()`) is the signal that the rest of the customer-dependent state has actually caught up, which is presumably why base itself waits for it rather than firing merge directly off the raw mutation promise.

Also corrected the same day: base additionally gates its own call on `hasBasketItem && prevAuthType === 'guest'` (via `useCustomerBaskets` + `usePrevious(customerType)`) — skip a pointless merge call when the guest basket is empty. This build deliberately does **not** replicate that guard (Marcel's call, 2026-09-19, asked directly): the `prevAuthType === 'guest'` half is already structurally guaranteed here for free — `handleTriggerClick` never opens this drawer at all when the customer is already registered, so every path that can reach the `isRegistered` effect's merge call started from a guest session by construction, with no `usePrevious` needed. The `hasBasketItem` half is deliberately skipped: replicating it would mean wiring a brand-new basket-loading dependency into a hook that has never needed one, on a step already flagged (pass criterion 4 below) as having no CODEOWNERS coverage to catch a subtle timing mistake — and the failure mode of getting that new dependency's timing wrong (merge silently skipped when it shouldn't be) is the exact "shopper's items are gone" bug this whole step exists to close. The failure mode of *not* having the check (one occasional harmless merge-call on an empty basket) is strictly cheaper. Call unconditionally inside the effect; no `useCustomerBaskets`, no `usePrevious`, no `customerType` needed.

`sum_quantities`, not the SDK default `higher_quantity`, because AC5's "combined quantity exceeds the maximum" only works if quantities add. **This changes every merge, not just over-max ones** — a guest adds one dress, signs in a week later, the account already had it: today they get one, with summing they get two. Marcel accepted this explicitly. It must go in a comment on SFCC-250 (deferred to post-build) because no AC describes it and a tester finding it otherwise has no way to know two items is intended.

**Pass criteria.**
1. `useWishlistAuthDrawer.test.tsx` asserts `mergeBasket` is called exactly once on passwordless success, with `productItemMergeMode: 'sum_quantities'` and `createDestinationBasket: true`.
2. It asserts `mergeBasket` is **not** called on the create-account route (base deliberately skips register).
3. It asserts the social-IDP route is untouched — no second merge added on top of base `social-login-redirect`'s.
4. **Regression gate on the other three consumers.** The hook is consumed by `header/rightBar`, `drawer-menu`, `product-view` and (new) the cart. Existing tests for all four still pass, and the PR body names all four as the change's blast radius. This is a shared hook with four call sites and **no CODEOWNERS entry** (see open question 3) — the review that would normally catch a mistake here is not automatically requested.
5. The hook's exported signature is **unchanged**. A signature change would need a team RFC (AGENTS.md "When to Stop").
6. Live verification is **deferred** per §7 — the code is in scope, the defect ticket and the live proof are not. Say so in the PR body so nobody reads the merge as verified.

#### Step 4.2 — `useCartMergeAndCap`

**Changes.** One shared function called by both the post-auth callback and the render guard — one implementation, not two copies.

Settled shape, all of it: threshold **`>=`** not `==` (a line already holding 4 must fail the check, or the `+` stays live exactly when it matters); scope is **per line item**, not per SKU (the SKU is already size + colour, so in normal shopping one line is one SKU); cap **consolidates to one line at 3** (free — `sum_quantities` already produces a single merged line item); callback order **merge → cap → 272's wishlist resume** (the wishlist move acts on a line the merge may have just consolidated and the cap just reduced; reversing it moves a quantity the shopper never saw); render guard is a secondary backstop that **no-ops while `useIsMutating()` is non-zero**, so it cannot race the callback; **keep the loop guard** — one correction in flight, one attempt per basket version, then stop and surface an error, because a write-on-render without it can rate-limit a shopper out of their own basket; **no action on the brief 4-then-3 flash** — observe real behaviour first.

**Pass criteria.**
1. Unit tests: line at 2 with max 3 → no change. Line at 3 → no change (`>=` boundary, the case `==` gets wrong is 4). Line at 4 → reduced to 3. Line at 5 → reduced to 3. Two lines of the same SKU at 2 each after a `sum_quantities` merge → one consolidated line at 3.
2. `useIsMutating()` non-zero → function returns without issuing a write. Asserted, not assumed.
3. Loop guard: two consecutive invocations against the **same** basket version issue exactly **one** write. A server rejection surfaces an error and does **not** retry indefinitely.
4. Callback order asserted: with all three armed, merge resolves before cap, and cap resolves before the wishlist resume. Assert on call order, not on final state — final state can look right with the wrong order.
5. Max value comes from `maxOrderQuantity.ts` (step 3.4), not a literal.
6. **State in the PR body that this is not end-to-end verifiable** until SFCC-268's `afterGET` hook is deployed (gate findings #1/#2 — the TSD is `v0.1 Draft`, Technical Lead sign-off Pending, and the live dev-sandbox probe found no `c_maxOrderQuantity` on any product, while Jira has 268 as Ready for SIT). 1	import { useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';
2	import type { ShopperBasketsV2Types } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
3	import { useShopperBasketsV2Mutation as useShopperBasketsMutation } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
4	import { getMaxOrderQuantity } from 'app/utils/maxOrderQuantity';
5	
6	/**
7	 * The minimal basket shape this hook needs, regardless of which caller supplies it: the
8	 * post-auth callback (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`, wired in this step) passes the resolved value
9	 * of its own `mergeBasket` mutation directly; the cart drawer's render guard
10	 * (`overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx`, step 4.6 — not yet built) will pass its
11	 * own `useCurrentBasket()` data. `Pick`-narrowed, matching `cartItemMapper.ts`'s own established
12	 * pattern for taking an untyped-at-the-edges SDK response and narrowing it to only the fields a
13	 * pure function actually reads, rather than depending on the exact generic SDK response type
14	 * either caller's own mutation/query hook happens to produce.
15	 */
16	export type CartCapBasket = Pick<ShopperBasketsV2Types.Basket, 'basketId' | 'lastModified' | 'productItems'>;
17	
18	/**
19	 * Outcome of one `capBasketQuantities` call. A discriminated union (typescript.md's guidance for
20	 * variant/state modelling) rather than a boolean-plus-optional-error: each branch is something a
21	 * caller could reasonably want to react to differently, and no AC or copy exists yet for any of
22	 * them (that is `useCartMessages`, step 4.3, not built) — this file only reports what happened,
23	 * it does not decide what the shopper sees.
24	 */
25	export type CartCapResult =
26	  | { status: 'not-needed' }
27	  | { status: 'skipped'; reason: 'mutation-in-flight' | 'already-attempted-this-version' }
28	  | { status: 'corrected' }
29	  | { status: 'error'; error: unknown };
30	
31	/**
32	 * `getMaxOrderQuantity` is typed for a SCAPI product response (`id: string` required — see
33	 * `overrides/app/utils/maxOrderQuantity.ts`). A basket line item has no `id` field at all: only
34	 * `itemId`/`productId` (confirmed against the generated `BasketProductItem` type — verified via
35	 * a throwaway `tsc` repro that assigning a same-shaped object to a type requiring `id` fails
36	 * with "Property 'id' is missing"), so passing one directly does not type-check, despite it
37	 * carrying the same `{[key: string]: any}` catch-all a real `c_maxOrderQuantity` value would
38	 * arrive through once SFCC-268 ships. `product-item/index.tsx` already lives with the identical
39	 * gap at its own `getMaxOrderQuantity(product)` call site (`type SfccProduct = any`, lines 171
40	 * and 331) — narrowed here with an explicit, commented cast instead of a bare `any` parameter,
41	 * per typescript.md's "no `any` without an inline comment" rule.
42	 */
43	const getLineMaxOrderQuantity = (item: ShopperBasketsV2Types.BasketProductItem): number =>
44	  getMaxOrderQuantity(item as unknown as Parameters<typeof getMaxOrderQuantity>[0]);
45	
46	/**
47	 * A line needs correction once its quantity exceeds the cap — i.e. once it reaches the smallest
48	 * over-cap value (`max + 1`; `4` when `max` is `3`) or anything above it. Written as `quantity >
49	 * max` rather than comparing against a separately-named `max + 1` boundary, but the two are the
50	 * same comparison: this must be a "the whole range above the boundary" check, not an
51	 * exact-equality check against a single value — an equality check against `max + 1` alone would
52	 * correctly catch a line at 4 but wrongly leave a line at 5 or more uncorrected, which is
53	 * observably wrong against this hook's own test fixture (a line at 5 must reduce to 3, not stay
54	 * at 5).
55	 */
56	const needsQuantityCorrection = (
57	  item: ShopperBasketsV2Types.BasketProductItem,
58	): item is ShopperBasketsV2Types.BasketProductItem & { quantity: number } =>
59	  typeof item.quantity === 'number' && item.quantity > getLineMaxOrderQuantity(item);
60	
61	/**
62	 * SFCC baskets carry no explicit version counter. `basketId` + `lastModified` change together on
63	 * every write SFCC accepts (both real fields on the generated `Basket` type), so the pair is a
64	 * workable proxy for "the exact basket state a correction was last attempted against" — this is
65	 * this file's own reasoned choice, not sourced from an existing codebase precedent or doc.
66	 */
67	const getBasketVersionKey = (basket: CartCapBasket): string => `${basket.basketId ?? ''}:${basket.lastModified ?? ''}`;
68	
69	/**
70	 * Storage key for "which basket version has a correction already been attempted against."
71	 * Deliberately not a `useRef` — the post-auth callback (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`) and the
72	 * future render guard (step 4.6) each get their own separate `useCartMergeAndCap()` call, and
73	 * therefore their own separate refs, since they mount in two different React component trees. A
74	 * plain ref cannot coordinate between them. Piggybacking on the already-global `QueryClient` (the
75	 * same one `capBasketQuantities`'s own mutation-in-flight guard reads from — see that function's
76	 * own comment) via `getQueryData`/`setQueryData` gives real cross-instance-shared storage without
77	 * inventing a new module-level singleton or Context provider. It is also, unlike a React-render-
78	 * time hook value, live/imperative — reading and then
79	 * immediately writing it inside `capBasketQuantities` with no `await` in between (see that
80	 * function) leaves no window for two near-simultaneous calls to both pass the check before either
81	 * has recorded its attempt, since JavaScript runs that synchronous read-then-write as one
82	 * uninterruptible step.
83	 */
84	const CAP_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY = ['zimmCartMergeAndCap', 'attemptedBasketVersion'] as const;
85	
86	export type UseCartMergeAndCapReturn = {
87	  /**
88	   * Checks every basket line against `getMaxOrderQuantity` and, if any line exceeds its cap,
89	   * issues one `updateItemsInBasket` write reducing every over-cap line to its own max in a
90	   * single request (matching the SFCC-11 plan's "one write" framing even when more than one line
91	   * needs correcting). Resolves only once that write — if one was issued — has fully settled, so
92	   * a caller sequencing merge -> cap -> a future wishlist-resume can `await` this in turn without
93	   * racing it.
94	   */
95	  capBasketQuantities: (basket: CartCapBasket) => Promise<CartCapResult>;
96	};
97	
98	/**
99	 * Hook — the shared "cap" half of SFCC-250's merge-then-cap flow. Two callers share this one
100	 * implementation, not two copies: the post-auth callback inside `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own
101	 * `isRegistered` effect (wired in this step, right after that effect's existing `mergeBasket`
102	 * call), and the cart drawer's render guard, which will live in
103	 * `overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx` (not yet built — a later step, 4.6, wires
104	 * that second call site; this hook is written to support it, not to assume it already exists).
105	 *
106	 * Per rules-of-hooks, call this at the top level of whichever hook or component needs it — never
107	 * from inside a `useEffect` callback — and invoke the returned `capBasketQuantities` function
108	 * itself from inside the effect/render path instead.
109	 *
110	 * @returns `capBasketQuantities`, the one function both callers invoke.
111	 */
112	export const useCartMergeAndCap = (): UseCartMergeAndCapReturn => {
113	  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
114	  const updateItemsInBasket = useShopperBasketsMutation('updateItemsInBasket');
115	
116	  const capBasketQuantities = async (basket: CartCapBasket): Promise<CartCapResult> => {
117	    // No-op while any mutation is in flight (this hook's own prior correction, the merge that
118	    // just ran, a shopper's manual quantity edit — anything) so this can never race a write
119	    // already under way. See this function's own JSDoc.
120	    //
121	    // REWORK (round 1, Tester-confirmed defect): this must be a LIVE read taken at the moment
122	    // this function actually runs — not a React-render-time value closed over at this hook's own
123	    // top level. `capBasketQuantities` is captured once by its caller and invoked later, from
124	    // inside an async callback (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s `mergeBasket.mutate(...).onSuccess`,
125	    // itself only reachable after a real network round trip) with no guarantee that hook instance
126	    // re-renders in between. A `useIsMutating()` value read at this hook's own top level (the
127	    // original approach here) would still reflect whatever mutation count existed at that earlier
128	    // render, not the real state at the moment this guard actually needs to check it.
129	    //
130	    // `queryClient.isMutating(filters?)` (confirmed against the installed
131	    // `@tanstack/query-core@4.43.0` source — a single deduped version across this project's whole
132	    // dependency tree, per `npm ls @tanstack/react-query` — `node_modules/@tanstack/query-core/
133	    // build/lib/queryClient.esm.js`: `isMutating(filters) { return this.mutationCache.findAll(
134	    // {...filters, fetching: true}).length; }`) computes this fresh from the live mutation cache
135	    // on every call. It is the exact same computation `useIsMutating()` itself wraps in
136	    // `useSyncExternalStore` for React reactivity (`node_modules/@tanstack/react-query/build/lib/
137	    // useIsMutating.esm.js`: `() => queryClient.isMutating(filters)`), just read directly instead
138	    // of through a render-synced subscription — so this preserves the exact same "every mutation
139	    // anywhere in the app" scope this guard has always had (commerce-sdk-react's basket mutation
140	    // hooks set no `mutationKey`, so an unscoped call is still the only reading that sees all of
141	    // them), it now just reads that scope live instead of stale.
142	    if (queryClient.isMutating() > 0) {
143	      return { status: 'skipped', reason: 'mutation-in-flight' };
144	    }
145	
146	    const correctedItems = (basket.productItems ?? []).filter(needsQuantityCorrection).map((item) => ({
147	      itemId: item.itemId,
148	      productId: item.productId,
149	      quantity: getLineMaxOrderQuantity(item),
150	    }));
151	
152	    if (correctedItems.length === 0) {
153	      return { status: 'not-needed' };
154	    }
155	
156	    if (!basket.basketId) {
157	      // No basketId means there is nothing valid to address a write at — surface this as an
158	      // error rather than silently doing nothing, so a caller can tell "nothing needed fixing"
159	      // apart from "something needed fixing and couldn't be".
160	      return { status: 'error', error: new Error('useCartMergeAndCap: basket is missing a basketId.') };
161	    }
162	
163	    const versionKey = getBasketVersionKey(basket);
164	    if (queryClient.getQueryData<string>(CAP_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY) === versionKey) {
165	      // Loop guard: a correction has already been attempted against this exact basket state,
166	      // whether it succeeded or failed — do not retry it. See CAP_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY's own
167	      // comment for why this is a live cache read rather than a per-instance ref, and why
168	      // setting it below, before the `await`, is what keeps this race-free.
169	      return { status: 'skipped', reason: 'already-attempted-this-version' };
170	    }
171	    queryClient.setQueryData(CAP_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY, versionKey);
172	
173	    try {
174	      await updateItemsInBasket.mutateAsync({
175	        parameters: { basketId: basket.basketId },
176	        body: correctedItems,
177	      });
178	      return { status: 'corrected' };
179	    } catch (error) {
180	      // Surfaced to the caller, not retried: the version is already marked attempted above, so a
181	      // later call against this same unchanged basket state returns 'skipped' rather than
182	      // hammering the server again — no retry storm.
183	      return { status: 'error', error };
184	    }
185	  };
186	
187	  return { capBasketQuantities };
188	};
189
